passages.text: As dead flies bring a stench to the perfumer’s oil, so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.
passages.sermon:
Dead flies cause the perfumer’s oil to stink.
A small amount of folly can ruin something valuable.
A little foolishness outweighs wisdom.
A little foolishness outweighs honor.
passages.original: זְב֣וּבֵי מָ֔וֶת יַבְאִ֥ישׁ יַבִּ֖יעַ שֶׁ֣מֶן רוֹקֵ֑חַ יָקָ֛ר מֵחָכְמָ֥ה מִכָּב֖וֹד סִכְל֥וּת מְעָֽט׃

passages.text: A wise man’s heart inclines to the right, but the heart of a fool to the left.
passages.sermon:
A wise man has a heart that turns to the right.
A wise man chooses what is good and true.
A fool has a heart that turns to the left.
A fool chooses what is wrong and foolish.
passages.original: לֵ֤ב חָכָם֙ לִֽימִינ֔וֹ וְלֵ֥ב כְּסִ֖יל לִשְׂמֹאלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Even as the fool walks along the road, his sense is lacking, and he shows everyone that he is a fool.
passages.sermon: A fool walks on the road.\r\nHe lacks sense in his heart.\r\nHe shows everyone that he is a fool.
passages.original: וְגַם־ בַּדֶּ֛רֶךְ כְּשֶׁהַסָּכָל הֹלֵ֖ךְ לִבּ֣וֹ חָסֵ֑ר וְאָמַ֥ר לַכֹּ֖ל סָכָ֥ל הֽוּא׃

passages.text: If the ruler’s temper flares against you, do not abandon your post, for calmness lays great offenses to rest.
passages.sermon:
A ruler may become angry with you.
Do not leave your position.
Stay where you are.
Remain calm.
Calmness can stop great offenses.
Calmness can bring peace.
passages.original: אִם־ ר֤וּחַ הַמּוֹשֵׁל֙ תַּעֲלֶ֣ה עָלֶ֔יךָ מְקוֹמְךָ֖ אַל־ תַּנַּ֑ח כִּ֣י מַרְפֵּ֔א יַנִּ֖יחַ חֲטָאִ֥ים גְּדוֹלִֽים׃

passages.text: There is an evil I have seen under the sun— an error that proceeds from the ruler: Folly is appointed to great heights, but the rich sit in lowly positions.
passages.sermon:
I have seen an evil under the sun.
This evil is an error that comes from the ruler.
Foolish people are given high positions.
Rich people sit in low places.
passages.original: יֵ֣שׁ רָעָ֔ה רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ כִּשְׁגָגָ֕ה שֶׁיֹּצָ֖א מִלִּפְנֵ֥י הַשַּׁלִּֽיט׃ נִתַּ֣ן הַסֶּ֔כֶל בַּמְּרוֹמִ֖ים רַבִּ֑ים וַעֲשִׁירִ֖ים בַּשֵּׁ֥פֶל יֵשֵֽׁבוּ׃

passages.text: I have seen slaves on horseback, while princes go on foot like slaves.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is an observer under the sun.
He has seen something unusual.
He has seen slaves riding on horses.
He has seen princes walking on the ground.
The princes walk like slaves.
passages.original: רָאִ֥יתִי עֲבָדִ֖ים עַל־ סוּסִ֑ים וְשָׂרִ֛ים הֹלְכִ֥ים כַּעֲבָדִ֖ים עַל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: He who digs a pit may fall into it, and he who breaches a wall may be bitten by a snake.
passages.sermon:
A person may dig a pit.
That person may fall into the pit he dug.
A person may break through a wall.
A snake may bite the person who breaks through the wall.
passages.original: חֹפֵ֥ר גּוּמָּ֖ץ בּ֣וֹ יִפּ֑וֹל וּפֹרֵ֥ץ גָּדֵ֖ר יִשְּׁכֶ֥נּוּ נָחָֽשׁ׃

passages.text: The one who quarries stones may be injured by them, and he who splits logs endangers himself.
passages.sermon: A person who quarries stones may be hurt by the stones.\r\nA person who splits logs puts himself in danger.
passages.original: מַסִּ֣יעַ אֲבָנִ֔ים יֵעָצֵ֖ב בָּהֶ֑ם בּוֹקֵ֥עַ עֵצִ֖ים יִסָּ֥כֶן בָּֽם׃

passages.text: If the axe is dull and the blade unsharpened, more strength must be exerted, but skill produces success.
passages.sermon:
A dull axe cannot cut well.
An unsharpened blade makes work harder.
A person must use more strength to cut with a dull axe.
Skill helps a person succeed.
Wisdom gives an advantage.
passages.original: אִם־ קֵהָ֣ה הַבַּרְזֶ֗ל וְהוּא֙ לֹא־ פָנִ֣ים קִלְקַ֔ל וַחֲיָלִ֖ים יְגַבֵּ֑ר וְיִתְר֥וֹן הַכְשֵׁ֖יר חָכְמָֽה׃

passages.text: If the snake bites before it is charmed, there is no profit for the charmer.
passages.sermon:
A snake may bite a person.
The snake may bite before anyone charms it.
A snake charmer tries to control the snake with words or music.
If the snake bites before the charmer acts, the charmer gains nothing.
The charmer cannot profit if he does not act in time.
passages.original: אִם־ יִשֹּׁ֥ךְ הַנָּחָ֖שׁ בְּלוֹא־ לָ֑חַשׁ וְאֵ֣ין יִתְר֔וֹן לְבַ֖עַל הַלָּשֽׁוֹן׃

passages.text: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious, but the lips of a fool consume him.
passages.sermon:
A wise man speaks with grace.
His words show kindness.
A fool speaks with his lips.
His own words destroy him.
passages.original: דִּבְרֵ֥י פִי־ חָכָ֖ם חֵ֑ן וְשִׂפְת֥וֹת כְּסִ֖יל תְּבַלְּעֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: The beginning of his talk is folly, and the end of his speech is evil madness.
passages.sermon:
A fool begins to speak.
He starts with foolish words.
He continues to speak.
He ends with words that are evil and mad.
His speech moves from folly to wickedness.
His words become more harmful as he goes on.
passages.original: תְּחִלַּ֥ת דִּבְרֵי־ פִ֖יהוּ סִכְל֑וּת וְאַחֲרִ֣ית פִּ֔יהוּ הוֹלֵל֖וּת רָעָֽה׃

passages.text: Yet the fool multiplies words. No one knows what is coming, and who can tell him what will come after him?
passages.sermon: A fool speaks many words.\r\nNo person knows what will happen in the future.\r\nNo one can tell a fool what will come after him.
passages.original: וְהַסָּכָ֖ל יַרְבֶּ֣ה דְבָרִ֑ים לֹא־ יֵדַ֤ע הָאָדָם֙ מַה־ שֶׁיִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר יִֽהְיֶה֙ מֵֽאַחֲרָ֔יו מִ֖י יַגִּ֥יד לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The toil of a fool wearies him, for he does not know the way to the city.
passages.sermon:
A fool works hard.
His work makes him tired.
He does not know the way to the city.
He cannot find the right path.
His lack of understanding causes his trouble.
passages.original: עֲמַ֥ל הַכְּסִילִ֖ים תְּיַגְּעֶ֑נּוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ יָדַ֖ע לָלֶ֥כֶת אֶל־ עִֽיר׃

passages.text: Woe to you, O land whose king is a youth, and whose princes feast in the morning.
passages.sermon:
A land suffers when its king is a young man.
The land also suffers when its princes eat in the morning.
A young king lacks experience.
Princes who feast early show a lack of discipline.
This brings trouble to the land.
passages.original: אִֽי־ לָ֣ךְ אֶ֔רֶץ שֶׁמַּלְכֵּ֖ךְ נָ֑עַר וְשָׂרַ֖יִךְ בַּבֹּ֥קֶר יֹאכֵֽלוּ׃

passages.text: Blessed are you, O land whose king is a son of nobles, and whose princes feast at the proper time— for strength and not for drunkenness.
passages.sermon:
A land is blessed when its king is the son of nobles.
The king comes from a noble family.
The princes of this land eat at the proper time.
They eat for strength.
They do not eat for drunkenness.
passages.original: אַשְׁרֵ֣יךְ אֶ֔רֶץ שֶׁמַּלְכֵּ֖ךְ בֶּן־ חוֹרִ֑ים וְשָׂרַ֙יִךְ֙ בָּעֵ֣ת יֹאכֵ֔לוּ בִּגְבוּרָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א בַשְּׁתִֽי׃

passages.text: Through laziness the roof caves in, and in the hands of the idle, the house leaks.
passages.sermon:
Laziness causes damage.
A lazy person allows the roof to cave in.
Idle hands let the house leak.
Neglect brings ruin to a home.
passages.original: בַּעֲצַלְתַּ֖יִם יִמַּ֣ךְ הַמְּקָרֶ֑ה וּבְשִׁפְל֥וּת יָדַ֖יִם יִדְלֹ֥ף הַבָּֽיִת׃

passages.text: A feast is prepared for laughter, and wine makes life merry, but money is the answer for everything.
passages.sermon: People prepare bread for laughter.\r\nWine brings joy to life.\r\nMoney provides for every need.
passages.original: לִשְׂחוֹק֙ עֹשִׂ֣ים לֶ֔חֶם וְיַ֖יִן יְשַׂמַּ֣ח חַיִּ֑ים וְהַכֶּ֖סֶף יַעֲנֶ֥ה אֶת־ הַכֹּֽל׃

passages.text: Do not curse the king even in your thoughts, or curse the rich even in your bedroom, for a bird of the air may carry your words, and a winged creature may report your speech.
passages.sermon:
Do not curse the king, even in your thoughts.
Do not curse the rich, even in your bedroom.
A bird of the air may carry your words.
A winged creature may report what you say.
passages.original: גַּ֣ם בְּמַדָּֽעֲךָ֗ מֶ֚לֶךְ אַל־ תְּקַלֵּ֔ל וּבְחַדְרֵי֙ מִשְׁכָּ֣בְךָ֔ אַל־ תְּקַלֵּ֖ל עָשִׁ֑יר כִּ֣י ע֤וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ יוֹלִ֣יךְ אֶת־ הַקּ֔וֹל וּבַ֥עַל הַכְּנָפַיִם יַגֵּ֥יד דָּבָֽר׃
